Chapter 1.title: Arjuna Vishada Yoga (The Yoga of Despondency of Arjuna)
Chapter 1.summary: Arjuna is overcome by sorrow and confusion as he prepares for battle. He is torn between his duty as a warrior and his emotional attachment to his family. Arjuna expresses his desire to abandon the war, setting the stage for Lord Krishna’s teachings.

Chapter 2.title: Sankhya Yoga (The Yoga of Knowledge)
Chapter 2.summary: Lord Krishna addresses Arjuna's despair, explaining the eternal nature of the soul, which is neither born nor dies. Krishna urges Arjuna to rise above his grief and introduces the philosophy of Sankhya, focusing on the distinction between the body and the soul (Atman).

Chapter 3.title: Karma Yoga (The Yoga of Action)
Chapter 3.summary: Krishna teaches the importance of performing one’s duties without attachment to the results. He explains that selfless action, performed in accordance with one’s duty, leads to spiritual growth and liberation.

Chapter 4.title: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga (The Yoga of Knowledge and Renunciation of Action)
Chapter 4.summary: Krishna explains the relationship between knowledge and action. He reveals that he incarnates in every age to restore righteousness and explains that performing actions in accordance with divine wisdom leads to liberation.

Chapter 5.title: Karma Sanyasa Yoga (The Yoga of Renunciation)
Chapter 5.summary: Krishna discusses renouncing the fruits of action versus renouncing action itself. He teaches that true renunciation is about detaching from the results of actions, not abandoning action itself. Selfless action leads to liberation.

Chapter 6.title: Dhyana Yoga (The Yoga of Meditation)
Chapter 6.summary: Krishna emphasizes the importance of meditation and mind control. He explains that a true yogi is one who has mastered self-discipline and can focus on the divine through meditation. Meditation leads to self-realization and union with the divine.

Chapter 7.title: Jnana Vijnana Yoga (The Yoga of Knowledge and Wisdom)
Chapter 7.summary: Krishna reveals the supreme knowledge of the self and the difference between the manifest and the unmanifest. He explains that surrendering to the divine and understanding the eternal truth leads to liberation.

Chapter 8.title: Aksara Brahma Yoga (The Yoga of the Imperishable Absolute)
Chapter 8.summary: Krishna explains the nature of the imperishable Brahman and the soul’s journey after death. He reveals the two paths—the bright path leading to liberation and the dark path leading to rebirth. The ultimate goal is liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Chapter 9.title: Raja Vidya Raja Guhya Yoga (The Yoga of Royal Knowledge and Royal Secret)
Chapter 9.summary: Krishna reveals the supreme knowledge and secret of the universe—that the divine pervades all beings and all things. By surrendering to the divine with devotion, one can attain liberation and self-realization.

Chapter 10.title: Vibhuti Yoga (The Yoga of Divine Glories)
Chapter 10.summary: Krishna reveals his divine manifestations in various forms in the universe. He explains that everything is a manifestation of his divine power, and those who recognize this knowledge deepen their devotion to the divine.

Chapter 11.title: Visvarupa Darshana Yoga (The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form)
Chapter 11.summary: Krishna grants Arjuna the divine vision to witness his universal form, a cosmic vision that reveals Krishna as the ultimate reality behind creation, destruction, and the cycle of life and death.

Chapter 12.title: Bhakti Yoga (The Yoga of Devotion)
Chapter 12.summary: Krishna explains the path of devotion as the easiest way to attain liberation. He describes the qualities of a true devotee and emphasizes the importance of single-minded devotion and surrender to the divine.

Chapter 13.title: Kshetra Kshetragna Vibhaga Yoga (The Yoga of the Field and the Knower of the Field)
Chapter 13.summary: Krishna explains the difference between the physical body (the field) and the soul (the knower of the field). He teaches that understanding the self leads to liberation and that the soul transcends the body and mind.

Chapter 14.title: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga (The Yoga of the Division of the Three Gunas)
Chapter 14.summary: Krishna explains the three gunas—sattva, rajas, and tamas—that govern human behavior. He teaches that transcending these gunas through devotion and self-discipline leads to liberation.

Chapter 15.title: Purusottama Yoga (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
Chapter 15.summary: Krishna reveals the supreme nature of the soul and explains that the eternal soul transcends both the material and spiritual realms. He emphasizes devotion and surrender to the supreme being as the ultimate goal of human life.

Chapter 16.title: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga (The Yoga of the Division Between the Divine and the Demoniacal)
Chapter 16.summary: Krishna contrasts the qualities of the divine and demoniacal nature, explaining that virtuous qualities lead to spiritual progress while evil qualities bind the soul to the material world.

Chapter 17.title: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga (The Yoga of the Threefold Faith)
Chapter 17.summary: Krishna explains the three types of faith corresponding to the three gunas. He teaches that faith, when aligned with devotion and purity, leads to spiritual growth and liberation.

Chapter 18.title: Moksha Sannyasa Yoga (The Yoga of Liberation and Renunciation)
Chapter 18.summary: Krishna summarizes his teachings, explaining the nature of liberation and selfless action. He urges Arjuna to perform his duties with devotion and detachment, concluding that liberation comes through selfless action and devotion.
